lines: If Hoover Dam were poured in one piece, it would still be cooling down today.
If Hoover Dam were poured in ONE piece, it would STILL be cooling down today.
The fix is still hidden inside the wall. But first, the river.
The fix is still HIDDEN inside the wall. But first, the river.
Engineers blasted four tunnels through the canyon, each fifty six feet wide, and sent the whole Colorado River around the site.
Engineers blasted FOUR tunnels through the canyon, each 56 FEET wide, and sent the whole Colorado River AROUND the site.
Then, the heat problem. Setting concrete gets hot. This wall is seven hundred twenty six feet tall, and six hundred sixty feet thick at the base.
Then, the HEAT problem. Setting concrete gets HOT. This wall is 726 FEET tall, and 660 FEET thick at the base.
Poured in one go, it would take a hundred and twenty five years to cool, and crack as it shrank.
Poured in one go, it would take 125 YEARS to cool, and CRACK as it shrank.
So they built it as about two hundred and fifteen columns, up to sixty feet square, rising five feet at a time.
So they built it as about 215 COLUMNS, up to 60 feet square, rising 5 FEET at a time.
Here's the hidden part. Inside every block ran steel cooling pipes. River water, then chilled water from a refrigeration plant, pulled the heat out.
Here's the HIDDEN part. Inside every block ran steel COOLING PIPES. River water, then CHILLED water from a refrigeration plant, pulled the heat out.
Then grout was forced into the pipes and the gaps between blocks, locking everything into one solid wall.
Then GROUT was forced into the pipes and the gaps between blocks, locking everything into ONE solid wall.
Hundreds of miles of that pipe are still inside. And there's enough concrete to pave a road from San Francisco to New York.
HUNDREDS of miles of that pipe are still inside. And there's enough concrete to pave a road from SAN FRANCISCO to NEW YORK.
So no, it's not one piece. And that's exactly why it's not still cooling today.
So no, it's NOT one piece. And that's exactly why it's not STILL cooling today.
Follow for a new wonder every day.
FOLLOW for a new wonder every day.
